history.summary: Large 1475 sqft 99yr 4BR at Costa Del Sol (D16) at $3.0M / $2034 PSF, 240m from the new Bayshore MRT (TE29). Standout 6.68% URA resale CAGR over a deep 168-txn series, with the just-opened Bayshore station finally fixing this seafront estate's long-standing accessibility gap.
history.rating_rationale: The low 415 score_1000 is misleading — it penalizes the $3M quantum and 99yr lease, but the fundamentals are strong: 6.68% resale CAGR backed by 168 transactions (very high confidence), 240m to the new Bayshore MRT (a genuine re-rating catalyst), seafront living, and entry only ~2% above the $1999 median. The real risk is supply — two adjacent 1,000+ unit estates (Bayshore Park, The Bayshore) compete for tenants/buyers — and $3M thins the pool. On balance the transit catalyst plus proven appreciation outweigh these.
red_flags: $3.0M quantum sits above the deepest buyer band — slower exit
Heavy nearby supply (Bayshore Park, The Bayshore, new Bayshore precinct launches) competes for tenants/buyers
2004 99yr lease (~78yr left) — lease decay on the back end
catalysts: Bayshore MRT (TE29) 240m away — direct TEL access, resolves the estate's accessibility weakness
6.68% URA resale CAGR over 168 txns — among the strongest, best-evidenced in the batch
Seafront/East Coast lifestyle premium and Bayshore precinct rejuvenation

history.summary: 4BR 2,045 sqft asking $4.5M / $2,200 psf — above the project 12-month high print ($2,170, set by a 1,346 sqft unit) and ~35-48% over verified large-unit comps (1,755 sqft sold Nov 2025 at $1,482 psf / $2.6M; recent large 4BRs ~$2.8M). Under current priors the one robust signal (cheap-vs-peers) reads expensive, the $4.5M quantum thins the exit pool, and ~70yr remaining lease (from 1997) is a binding decay headwind into a 10,000+-home Bayshore supply wave.
history.rating_rationale: Verified via 99.co/Homejourney/EdgeProp aggregates: 12-mo transacted PSF $1,482-$2,170 (avg ~$1,884); large units trade at the LOW end, yet this large unit asks $2,200 psf — a decisive premium, not value. Prior 06-08 Buy (different $3.0M/1,475sqft unit) leaned on 6.68% trailing CAGR, which backtests show has ~0 forward power. Bayshore MRT (operational 2024) is already priced; the pending precinct pipeline (Bayshore Drive GLS ~1,280 units, Vela Bay 515 units, ~10k homes total) adds resale/rental competition over a 5-7yr hold. Algo 201 reflects legitimate penalties. Confidence medium not high: project fundamentals are sound and a deep negotiation toward ~$1,600-1,700 psf would change the math — but at asking this is an Avoid.
red_flags: Asking $2,200 psf exceeds the 12-mo high print and is ~35-48% above large-unit comps (1,755sqft @ $1,482 psf, Nov 2025)
$4.5M quantum materially thins the exit buyer pool
~70yr lease remaining (from 1997) — accelerating decay over hold + exit horizon
Bayshore precinct ~10,000-12,500 new homes (Bayshore Drive GLS, Vela Bay 2026) — direct supply competition
Trailing 6.68% CAGR (prior Buy rationale) has ~0 forward power under v3.4+ backtests
catalysts: Bayshore MRT TE29 240m away — real but operational since 2024, largely priced in
Bayshore precinct rejuvenation (retail, integrated hub) lifts the locale long-term
OCR/D16 region carries the strongest realized forward baseline (+3.7%/yr)
history.source: re-eval under v3.4.1+ priors (2026-06-11 loop iter 6; supersedes 2026-06-08 pre-prior-fix Buy on a different $3.0M unit)
